newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan president, Uzbek warlord meet in north.
newsitem.headline: Afghan president, Uzbek warlord meet in north.

text.p: Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani and Uzbek warlord Abdul Rashid Dostum embraced on a windswept stretch of highway east of Mazar-I-Sharif on Tuesday and began to explore forming a common front against Taleban forces.
It was the first meeting between Rabbani and Dostum in three years. Rivalry between Dostum and Rabanni's military commander, Ahmad Shah Masood, led Dostum to split from the government in 1994.

General Dostum told reporters that Masood was also expected in Mazar-I-Sharif by Wednesday. Dostum aides said virtually every leader of an anti-Taleban faction would be arriving in Mazar-I-Sharif, including a representative of the Afghan king in exile.
"Masood will come today or if he cannot make it today then tomorrow," Dostum told reporters as he waited for Rabbani to arrive on the highway.

The gathering in Mazar-I-Sharif leant support to a statement by Afghanistan's ambassador to India who told a news conference that Dostum had sent a message announcing support for Rabbani, whose government fled Kabul ahead of the Taleban advance.
"He (Dostum) is also in the coalition government of President Rabbani...I am informed they have come together," Ambassador Masood Khalili told reporters in New Delhi.
Rabbani shook hands with about 50 of the several hundred dignitaries who had queued along the highway to meet him.

The president then climbed into Dostums's black limousine with dark-tinted windows and the two men drove 30-minutes to Kala Jangy, west of the city, where Dostum forces occupy a picturesque mud-walled fortress originally built in the 19th century.

Hundreds of smartly-uniformed and well-armed Dostum soldiers stood at attention in front of other military bases along the two mens' route in a demonstration of the military might which Rabbani desperately needs to tap to bring the Taleban to heel.
Inside Kala Jangy fortress Rabanni and Dostum met for about 20 minutes, then broke for lunch.
Press aides to Dostum said there probably would be no statements from anyone involved in the meeting until Wednesday at the earliest.
"So far they have just met at a protocol level and there have been no substantive discussions," said one Dostum aide who asked not to be named.
"There is so much to discuss and there are so many other people expected to come to join them that it would not be fair to make any statement now."
Rank-and-file soldiers patrolling the ramparts of the fortress at Kala Jangy put a different gloss on the meeting.

They said it was now just a matter of time until Dostum, Rabbani, Masood and other former fixtures of the government which took control of Afghanistan when mujahideen forces captured Kabul in 1992, joined forces and turned on the Taleban.
"There could be a very great war now," said Rahmen, a Dostum soldier.
"General Dostum was the key to Kabul in 1992 and now he will be the key again. Dostum and Masood together would defeat the Taleban."
Dostum defected to the mujahideen from the government forces of President Najibullah just days before Kabul fell in 1992.
